title: Internal abelian ring sheaves have ring-valued presentations
statement: Let C be a category with topology J, whose object and morphism universes are bounded by the coefficient universe, with abelian sheafification and its monoidal localization [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every monoid R in abelian J-sheaves there is a J-sheaf A of rings and an isomorphism Mon.mk(forget_Ring_to_Ab A)≅R. No commutativity of R is assumed.

source.place: Tag 00YV, sheaves of rings and modules; sectionwise algebraic structures

proof.text: For a monoid in abelian groups, define multiplication by its tensor multiplication on pure tensors and the unit by its unit evaluated on 1. The ring axioms follow from the monoid and bilinearity axioms. Applying the ring-to-monoid construction recovers the original monoid: multiplication is checked on pure tensors; the integer unit is checked using additivity and integer multiples of 1. This gives a natural recovery isomorphism. The sectionwise ring construction is already implemented in InternalAbelianSheafModule.monToRing.

source.place: Tag 00YV, sheaves of rings and modules; sectionwise algebraic structures

proof.text: Apply the recovery construction to the monoid presheaf underlying R. Its abelian presheaf is definitionally the original sheaf, so forgetting along RingCat→Ab detects its sheaf condition. Form the ring-valued sheaf A. Use the equivalence between monoids in a functor category and functors to monoids to lift the sectionwise recovery isomorphism. Sheafify it monoidally; the monoidal sheafification counit gives the final isomorphism to R. This also works for the zero ring and the empty site.

lean.statement:
theorem internal_ring_sheaf_presentation
    {C : Type v} [Category.{w} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [UnivLE.{max v w, u}] [HasSheafify J Ab.{u}]
    [(J.W (A := Ab.{u})).IsMonoidal]
    (R : Mon (Sheaf J Ab.{u})) :
    ∃ A : Sheaf J RingCat.{u},
      Nonempty (Mon.mk ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ RingCat.{u} Ab.{u})).obj A) ≅ R)
